one_liner: Salesforce B2C Commerce offers broad REST APIs (SCAPI) with OAuth-style tokens (SLAS, Account Manager). Real use needs a B2C Commerce instance and per-merchant API clients. A demo sandbox and on-demand sandboxes are mentioned, but the pages don't show how to get one without a customer relationship.
auth_notes: Shopper APIs use SLAS (OAuth 2.1) with private client ID/secret. Admin APIs use an Account Manager token. Each merchant must create its own API client.
access_notes: The pages say the API is free for B2C Commerce customers, so it's tied to owning an instance. A shared demo sandbox and on-demand sandboxes are mentioned. The pages don't show whether an individual can get credentials for them without a customer realm. Low confidence; the draft's sales-contact quote came from a page that was not fetched, so it was dropped.
blocker_notes: Needs a B2C Commerce instance (customer-owned or on-demand sandbox) and a per-customer Account Manager or SLAS client. The pages don't settle whether a free self-serve path exists.

evidence.quote: The B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) is a set of RESTful APIs for building storefronts, merchant tools, and integrations on the B2C Commerce platform.
They use a SLAS private client to get a guest token, then fetch a product from the demo sandbox.
Use the [SCAPI Admin APIs](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/authorization-for-admin-apis.html) with an Account Manager token.
For B2C Commerce customers, the API is available at no extra cost.
If you don’t have a B2C Commerce instance, try the demo sandbox used in the example above.
To explore SCAPI with your assistant, use the [B2C MCP](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/b2c-developer-tooling.html#connect-your-ai-assistant).
